newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanians drink smuggled, cheaper scotch whisky.
newsitem.headline: Romanians drink smuggled, cheaper scotch whisky.

text.p: Romanians drink more than a million litres of Scotch whisky per year, but all but a tiny fraction of it is smuggled into the country, the business weekly Capital said on Thursday.

Capital said estimates by the Association of Scotch Whisky Producers which showed that Romania legally imported the equivalent of 9,900 litres of Scotch last year. It quoted consumption in 1995 at 1.3 million litres.

"High duties are an open invitation to tax evasion and smuggling," Angela Lepadatu, a representative of Britain's United Distillers told Capital. "The higher the duties, the more creative the smugglers become."
According to Capital, Romanians pay an average $12 for a bottle in shops.

With average monthly salaries of less than $80, few could afford a legally imported bottle priced at what trade specialists say costs about $60 when 85 percent customs duty and 200 percent excise duties are properly applied.
